newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: EU gives go-ahead for Palestine trade deal.
newsitem.headline: EU gives go-ahead for Palestine trade deal.

text.p: European Union Foreign Ministers gave the go-ahead on Tuesday for negotiation of a lucrative trade deal with Palestinians in the West Bank and Gaza Strip.

Foreign Ministers approved a proposal by the European Commission -- the EU's Executive -- for Palestinian authorities to be included in the so-called Euromed accord, which governs the 15-nation bloc's relations with Mediterranean partners.

The timing of the mandate will be seen as a boost for Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat as he prepares for a U.S.-led peace summit in Washington later on Tuesday with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Jordan's King Hussein.

The summit was called by U.S. President Bill Clinton to try to salvage a Middle East peace process threatened by a week of fighting sparked by Israel's opening of an archaeological tunnel under the Temple Mount in Jerusalem -- a site holy to both Jews and Moslems.

The Euromed Accord -- which aims to turn the Mediterranean region into a free-trade zone -- offers lucrative trade and financial incentives to non-EU countries in order to bring their economies into line with the 15-nation bloc.
The mandate given to the commission to negotiate Palestinian inclusion means the fledgling Palestinian state could be included by the end of this year.

The EU is the biggest donor of financial aid to Palestinian authorities and since 1993 has contributed over 320 million ecu European currency units ($400 million) to development of the West Bank and Gaza Strip.
This assistance will continue until 1988 with the EU committed to at least 50 million ecu a year in further development grants.
